cells.tense: You are here in the middle of it, pen in hand, and the shape is holding.
cells.act: walk the route with someone who is lost on it
cells.ask: Someone is stuck on ground you already crossed. Give them the way you went — out loud, once, start to finish. Then stop. What they do with it next is theirs.
cells.core:
You can work inside a question without needing the whole answer before you move. You have enough light for the next step, and you take it, and the step after that only shows up once you're standing in the next spot. That's how you find the shape of things. You're beside something you built, and it's holding.

Somebody else is stuck on the same stretch you already got through. Tell them the way you went — not to fix them, not to check how they take it, just put it where they can see it and stop. The part that's yours is saying it plainly, once, and then your hands come off it. That part does not need watching to count.
cells.sheetLine: You can work inside the question without demanding the whole road.
cells.verb: raising a first structure from what the clearing left
cells.place: the half-lit room where the next step is visible and the road is not

cells.tense: You are standing out past the thing you're building, spending a structure that isn't up yet.
cells.act: cross over to the people it actually requires
cells.ask: Go to the people this actually requires — the ones who'd have to build it with you. Show them the unfinished version you're holding. Let their hands in before it's decided.
cells.core:
You can picture something before it exists, and that's the gift. Lately the picturing has run past the making. You're tracing lines that haven't been raised, and each trace makes them feel more solid than they are. From inside, it feels like diligence. Anyone watching would call it work on a thing nobody signed up for yet.

A real structure is raised by more than one pair of hands. Yours is the first pair, not the only one. Go to the people this actually requires and show them the unfinished version in your head, and you learn which parts are shared and which are only yours. That's how you get through. You can't arrive at it by drawing alone. What you drew has to meet them.

cells.tense: You are still at a door that closed and moved on without you.
cells.act: decide it and act the same day, without explaining
cells.ask: Decide one thing about what you're building — the one you keep circling — and do it the same day. Don't explain it to anyone. Let the doing be the whole of it.
cells.core:
Something got cleared, and you're standing in the cleared space with the pen down. What's here is shape without a shape yet, and the wish to make something from it hasn't turned into a decision. So the space has been clean and empty and waiting. That's where you are. Not failure. Not finished. The cleared ground is real, and it's had nobody standing on it making calls.

Start smaller than the whole thing. One call about what gets raised here, done the same day, no explanation after. The call doesn't need to be right, it needs to be made, because a first decision is what turns a clearing into a site. You'll know it's working when the shape stops being something you circle and starts being something you carry. The clear space becomes a place once you put a stake in it.

cells.tense: You have the pen down on a page you are already writing, and you call it the room's handwriting.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: Keep your heading the next time it gets contested. Pick one choice about what you're building that you'd have called only sensible, and hold it steady when someone pushes — even a slight push. Don't argue. Just don't fold.
cells.core:
You are already making the calls. Where the shape is forming, the lines are your lines — you chose the pace, the direction, the version that went forward. Ask and you'd say you just did the obvious thing. The obvious thing was yours, and it's still being filed under circumstance.

The reason it matters isn't credit. It's that a structure defended by nobody gets blown over by the first strong opinion. Defend the heading once — not to win, just to keep the direction that was already chosen. When someone pushes on it, hold your ground steady. You'll find the direction was chosen by somebody, and the somebody has your name.
cells.sheetLine: The calls are yours, filed under just sensible.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is 'building something with others' — the record says Formation is collaborative construction at the formative scale, but nothing says the reader has co-builders in this specific part of their life; a reader could reasonably say 'I'm working this out alone.' The ask survives being wrong: showing someone the way you found is useful even if nobody is building beside them, because the showing is the act, not the being built-with. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the first cell's closing offer — 'let them hold the next piece themselves' — it is a nice line and it puts a condition on their care; cut it and let the cell end on what the person does.
